correctness.rationale: The total-reality hypothesis can indeed be removed from Campbell's proof. For a sparse noninteger real parameter \(a\), Campbell's lemmas first exclude \(a\in(0,1)\). If a nontrivial conjugate \(a^\ast\) is nonreal, then it is automatically outside the real compact set \([0,1]\cup\{a\}\); if it is real but not in \((0,1)\), irreducibility excludes the endpoints \(0,1\), so it is again outside that set. This replaces the sole load-bearing use of total reality in Campbell's proof. The remaining transfinite-diameter argument, the identification of complete conjugacy classes in the compact set with only \(0,1\), and the auxiliary polynomial contradiction then run unchanged. Pinch's real discreteness-to-algebraic-integrality input and the Fenner--Green--Homer strong-PV uniform-discreteness theorem supply the two outer implications.

originality.rationale: Campbell proves the necessity direction only under the explicit additional assumption that \(a\) is totally real. Inspection of the complete proof shows that this hypothesis is used to declare the chosen bad conjugate real before excluding it from \([0,1]\); a nonreal conjugate is already excluded from that real set, so the argument extends. Fenner, Green and Homer formulate the strong-PV discreteness converse as an open conjecture and prove the strong-PV sufficiency. Current Resultary search returned only the assigned all-real-parameter resolution and no broader prior theorem. The audited result therefore genuinely enlarges the published theorem and resolves the full real-parameter necessity, rather than merely specializing an existing statement.
